ChannelPreviewAuthorKind.description:
Who a preview's message reads as. `author_id` means a different thing for
each: a user id, a webhook id, a feed id, or (for an anonymous message the
viewer may not unmask) the `anon:{channel_id}:{alias}` pseudo-id that the
message itself carries. Only `user` ids name a member.

ChannelPreviewMedia.description:
The first attachment of a preview's message, so a row can lead with a
thumbnail. The client builds the file URL from `attachment_id`.

ChannelPreview.description:
The newest message of one guild channel, for the channel row of the
places panel (`GET /api/v1/guilds/{guild_id}/channel-previews`).

`content` is the message's raw text (markdown and `<@id>` tokens intact)
with whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces, cut to at most 140
characters including a trailing `…` when `truncated`; a cut never ends
inside a `<…>` token. Rendering (mentions, spoilers, emphasis) is the
client's job. It is null for an encrypted message, whose body the server
cannot read, and for a message without text (only media or a sticker).
A poll's text is its question (`message_type` 20).
`media` is null for an encrypted message as well.

author_name.description:
Guild nickname, else display name, else username; the webhook, feed or
anonymous alias for those kinds. Null when the author record is gone.

The version changes with every upload. This server always sends it; it
is optional in the contract because servers older than 3.2 (no banners)
leave it out of the summary, and absent reads exactly as null.

the contract for protocol-version tolerance: a server from before

picked) and as "this server cannot store a color".

VoiceMode.description:
How a member takes part in a voice channel. `listen` hears the voices and
never sends; everyone in the channel sees the member as listening in.

can_publish.description:
Whether the relay now accepts this member's media. `joined` without the
SPEAK permission is still `false`.

VoiceMode.description:
How a member takes part in a voice channel. `listen` hears the voices and
never sends; everyone in the channel sees the member as listening in.

VoiceStateSnapshot.description:
A voice state as READY lists it (`guilds[].voice_states[]`) and as a
`VOICE_STATE_UPDATE` for someone *in* a channel carries it. (A leave is
`channel_id: null` plus `prior_channel_id` and is not this shape.)

joined_at.description:
When the member entered this channel (RFC 3339), for "live 12 min" on a
room: the room started at the earliest `joined_at` among its members.
Stamped on every join and listen join, kept while the member stays in
the channel, reset by a move. Null only on a status announcement whose
stored row could not be read.

mode.description:
`listen` shows as "Listening in" on the roster.

`mode`, `self_stream_started_at` and `joined_at` are always sent by this
server. They are optional in the contract for protocol-version
tolerance: servers from before them leave them out. An
absent `mode` is `joined` (there was no listening in); an absent time is
unknown, exactly as null, and a client shows nothing it would have
derived from it (a room reads "live", not "live N min").

self_stream_started_at.description:
When the member's current stream started (RFC 3339), for "LIVE 42 MIN".
Non-null exactly while `self_stream` is true (when sent at all).

VoiceStateSnapshot.title: VoiceStateSnapshot

VoiceViewKind.description:
What a view session receives.

- `watch`: the chosen stream's video and its own audio (never the voices).
  Counted in the channel's watcher counts, so others see "2 watching".
- `ambient`: the stream's lowest simulcast layer, keyframes only, at most
  one frame a second, video only. Not counted and not shown to anybody.

VoiceViewMedia.description:
How to connect a view session's media (the same native endpoint a call
uses; the token admits only this view).

VoiceViewSession.description:
Response of `POST /api/v2/voice/{channel_id}/view`.

When the caller is already in this channel's call (joined or listening),
the view rides that call: `via_membership` is true, `session_id` and
`media` are null, and the caller subscribes to the stream through its call
connection. Otherwise it is a separate view session with its own receipt
and media credentials; an account holds one at a time, and a new one
replaces the old (whose connection the relay closes).
